## [0.22.0] - 2026-10-16

### Added

- **HTTP Client: Debug Request.** `HTTP: Debug Request at Caret` (also **Debug Request** in a `.http` file's
  right-click menu, and Debug on a `.http` file) sends the request with its pre-request scripts and response
  handlers under the JavaScript debugger. A script stops at its breakpoints, with the call stack, variables,
  watches and stepping of any JavaScript session, and the request goes on when you continue.
  - **Breakpoints go on the lines of a `{% %}` block** in the `.http` file itself, or in a `./check.js` handler
    file. Elsewhere in a `.http` file the toggle says why it doesn't set one.
  - It needs JavaScript debugging, as for a `.js` file: Settings → Debugging and vscode-js-debug.
  - A paused script is not stopped by the script timeout. A script whose debugger doesn't attach within 30
    seconds is stopped. Restart doesn't send the request again: run Debug Request again.
  - The script runs as usual — trusted folder, minimal environment, Node's permission model — and Node's
    inspector is allowed only for this, on a random port on 127.0.0.1. Letting a debugger in under the permission
    model needs Node.js 24.12 or later: on an older Node a debugged script runs without the permission model, and
    the Debug console, the status bar and the response's warnings say so.
- **HTTP Client: pre-request scripts.** A `< {% … %}` block or a `< ./sign.js` line above a request runs on
  Node.js before the request is resolved and sent.
  - **`request.variables.set(name, value)`** sets a variable for that request only. It wins over every other
    variable, including the file's `@name = value` lines.
  - **The request as far as it resolves:** `request.url`, `request.headers` and `request.body` (with
    `tryGetSubstituted()` and `getRaw()`), and `request.environment.get`.
  - **Signing:** the JetBrains `crypto` API (`crypto.sha256()`, `crypto.hmac.sha256().withTextSecret(…)`, md5,
    sha1, sha384, sha512, sha3, then `updateWithText`/`updateWithHex`/`updateWithBase64` and
    `digest().toHex()`/`toBase64()`), and `jwt.sign`/`verify`/`decode` (HS, RS, PS and ES algorithms with a
    secret or a PEM key).
  - **Global headers:** `client.global.headers.set(name, value)`, in a pre-request script or a response handler,
    adds a header to later requests (and, from a pre-request script, to its own request). A request's own header
    wins, a `Host` header is never set, and `clear(name)` removes one.
  - A request whose pre-request script cannot run — an untrusted folder, no Node.js, an error, a timeout — is
    **not sent**, and says why. The rest of a Run All still runs. `client.exit()` ends the script and sends the
    request. The script's tests and log come first in the Tests block.
  - **Secrets:** a script's values are sent as written, never resolved, so a script cannot make a request read
    `$env`/`$dotenv`. Scripts don't see secrets either: `request.environment.get` returns environment values as
    written, so keep signing keys in `http-client.private.env.json`. When a request that reads a secret goes to a
    host made of a script's or an earlier response's value, the secrets prompt names "a host chosen by an earlier
    response or a script".
- **Run with Trace for shell scripts.** `Run: Run with Trace` (palette, Run menu, and the editor's right-click
  menu on a shell script) runs the script with `-x`, keeping its shebang's interpreter and flags. Under bash
  each traced line names its file and line (`+/path/deploy.sh:12: cmd`) and is a link to that line; `sh` and
  dash trace without locations, and zsh is not supported. Putting `-x` in a run configuration's Interpreter
  options gives the same links. Trace lines are drawn muted, not as errors.
- **Modelines set the language** of a file whose name says nothing: a vim modeline (`# vim: ft=sh`,
  `vim: set filetype=bash :`) in the first or last five lines, or an emacs `-*- mode: sh -*-` line.
- **Terminal sessions in Markdown.** ```` ```console ```` and ```` ```shell-session ```` blocks in the preview show
  a muted prompt, a highlighted command and plain output. ```` ```shellscript ```` blocks are highlighted as shell.
- **Problems rows show the rule code** (`[SC2086]`), with **Open Rule Documentation** and **Copy Code** in their
  context menu.
- **Shell scripts: ShellCheck and shfmt.** bash-language-server needs both for linting and formatting, and
  without them it silently did neither. Doctor and Settings → LSP (Bash) now show whether each one is found,
  with an **Install** button, and the palette has `Install: ShellCheck and shfmt`. Editora downloads the
  official release binary for your platform, checks it against a SHA-256 hash built into Editora, and points
  the Bash server at it; a path you set yourself still wins. Opening a script without ShellCheck says so once,
  and Format Document without shfmt says shfmt is missing instead of "Already formatted". The server's own
  warnings now reach the Debug Log.
- **bash-language-server settings.** The Bash card in Settings → LSP sets ShellCheck's path and arguments
  (for example `--severity=warning` or `-x`), shfmt's path, dialect and style switches, the number of files
  the server analyses in the background (500 by default), workspace-wide symbols, and an explainshell
  endpoint for option hovers (empty by default). A project's `.editora/settings.json` can override them with
  a `bashIde` object that uses the server's own key names; paths and the explainshell endpoint need a trusted
  folder.
- **Shell run configurations have Interpreter and Interpreter options fields**, which override the
  interpreter the script's shebang names.
- **End Input for a running program.** The Run console has an End Input button, and Ctrl+D on an empty
  input line does the same, so a `while read` loop or `cat` can finish without Stop.
- **Folding for shell scripts:** functions, `{ }`, `if … fi`, loops, `case … esac` and each multi-line case
  item, multi-line `( )` and `$( )`, and here-docs. Sticky scroll now pins shell functions and blocks too.
- **A notice for shell scripts with Windows line endings or a byte-order mark**, which bash cannot run, with
  a Convert to LF (or Remove BOM) action. Running such a script first asks whether to convert it.
- **HTTP Client: response handlers, tests and checks.**
  - **JavaScript response handlers** — `> {% … %}` after a request, or `> ./check.js` — now run, on your own
    Node.js, once the response arrives. They use the JetBrains API: `client.test`, `client.assert`,
    `client.log`, `client.global`, `client.exit`, `response.body` (parsed JSON), `response.status`,
    `response.headers.valueOf`, `response.contentType`, `response.cookies()`, the request as sent
    (`request.url`, `request.headers`, `request.body`), `request.environment.get` and `jsonPath(…)`.
  - **A Tests block** in the response view lists each test with ✓ or ✗ and why it failed, then the handler's log
    and any error, with its line in the `.http` file. A `✓ 3 passed · ✗ 1 failed` badge sits beside the status
    line, Run All's summary counts the requests whose tests failed, and History rows carry a ✓ or ✗. Test
    results are kept in the saved history.
  - **Checks without JavaScript:** `# @assert status == 200`, `# @assert $.items[0].id == 7`,
    `# @assert header Content-Type contains json`, `# @assert $.token exists` (also `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`,
    `matches`, `!exists`, and `time`/`body` subjects), and `# @capture token = $.token`. They need neither
    Node.js nor a trusted folder.
  - **Session variables:** what `client.global.set` or `@capture` stores is used by later requests as
    `{{name}}` — after a Run All's earlier request, or a single run of it. It wins over the environment and loses
    to the file's own `@name = value`, is inserted as is (never resolved), and is cleared when the environment
    changes. The editor no longer marks `{{name}}` unresolved when the file sets it this way.
  - **Safety:** a handler is code from the folder, so it runs only from a trusted folder (the same trust as build
    scripts and secrets), asked once per run with Cancel as the default button. Node.js is started without your
    environment variables (so `process.env` cannot read a token around the secrets prompt) and, on Node.js 20 or
    later, under its permission model: no file writes, no child processes, no workers. It is stopped after 10
    seconds. A secret the request read reaches the handler masked. Handlers may make network requests. Remote
    `.http` files still do not run. Import cURL writes body lines the format would not send (from a `>`, `<>` or
    `###` line on) as comments, so a pasted command can never add a handler.
  - **Settings → Web:** turn handlers off, choose the Node.js to use, and set the timeout. The Doctor has a row
    for it. Pre-request scripts (`< {% %}`) are still skipped with a warning.
- **Emacs registers.** In the Emacs keymap:
  - `C-x r s` copies the selection into a register; with `C-u`, it cuts it.
  - `C-x r i` inserts a register's text, leaving the cursor before it.
  - `C-x r SPC` saves the cursor's file and position in a register.
  - `C-x r j` jumps back to that position, opening the file if it is closed.

  Each command takes the register's name as the next key; Escape cancels. A saved position follows edits
  to its file while the file is open. `Edit: List Registers` shows them all. Registers last for the
  session, one set per window, and every command is also in the palette.
- **More text tools, in the String Manipulation picker and the command palette.**
  - **Encode and decode the selected text:** Base64, URL encoding, JSON string escapes, HTML entities, and
    `\uXXXX` escapes. They work on every selection at once. A decode that cannot read one selection changes
    nothing.
  - **`Edit: Increment Number` / `Edit: Decrement Number`:** change the number at each cursor, or the next
    one on its line. They handle negatives, zero padding (`007` → `008`) and hexadecimal (`0x0f` → `0x10`);
    `C-u N` steps by N. In Emacs they are bound to `C-c =` and `C-c -`.
  - **`Edit: Keep Lines Matching…` / `Edit: Remove Lines Matching…`:** filter lines with a regular
    expression.
  - **Two more sorts:** case-sensitive, and natural order with duplicates removed.
- **Several rulers, rulers per language, and indent guides.** Settings → Editor now takes a list of ruler
  columns (`80, 120`) and, per language, lists that replace it (`java: 100; python: 79, 88`; a language with
  nothing after its colon has no rulers). The palette has `Editor: Set Rulers…` and `Editor: Set Rulers for
  This Language…`. An `.editorconfig` `max_line_length` still sets the first ruler, and `off` still hides them.
  **Indent guides** — faint vertical lines at each indentation level, carried through blank lines — are on by
  default. Turn them off with `View: Toggle Indent Guides` or in Settings → Editor. They are hidden in Zen and
  Simple UI and in large-file mode, follow the theme, and skip folded lines. They are placed from the text as
  it is laid out, so they stay on their columns when the line numbers gain a digit or are toggled, when the
  font changes, in a proportional font, and in a tab-indented file; scrolled sideways, they are not drawn over
  the line numbers. The ruler toggle is now `View: Toggle Rulers`.
- **Line commands, at every cursor.**
  - `Edit: Insert Line Below` (`Ctrl+Enter`) opens a new, indented line under the current one, wherever
    the cursor is on it. `Edit: Insert Line Above` (`Ctrl+Shift+Enter`) opens one above.
  - `Edit: Delete Line` (`Ctrl+Shift+K`, IntelliJ's `Ctrl+Y`) deletes the line or every selected line
    without touching the clipboard or the kill ring. Emacs' Kill Whole Line is unchanged.
  - `Edit: Select Line` (`Ctrl+L`) selects the line, and grows by a line each time.
  - `Edit: Indent Lines` / `Edit: Outdent Lines` (`Ctrl+]` / `Ctrl+[`) shift the line or selection by the
    file's indent unit, wherever the cursor is.

  Each runs at every cursor as one undo step, opens a collapsed fold before changing it, and renumbers an
  ordered Markdown list it changes. Keys are in the VS Code and Sublime keymaps, partly in CUA and IntelliJ
  (`⌘` on macOS); Delete Line is also in the Edit menu.
- **More ways to place multiple cursors.**
  - `Edit: Split Selection into Lines` turns each selected line into its own selection (Sublime's
    `Ctrl+Shift+L`; also in the Edit menu).
  - `Edit: Add Carets to Line Ends` puts a cursor at the end of every selected line (VS Code's and CUA's
    `Shift+Alt+I`, IntelliJ's `Alt+Shift+G`).
  - `Edit: Skip Occurrence` moves the newest selection on to the next match instead of adding one, wrapping
    round to the start (`Ctrl+K Ctrl+D` in VS Code and Sublime).
  - `Edit: Remove Last Added Caret` takes back the cursor added last (`Ctrl+U` in VS Code and Sublime,
    IntelliJ's `Alt+Shift+J`).

  In the Sublime keymap, `Select All Occurrences` moves to Sublime's own `Alt+F3` (`Ctrl+Cmd+G` on macOS),
  freeing `Ctrl+Shift+L` for Split into Lines.
- **Save All, Revert File and Reopen Closed Tab.** `File: Save All` saves every modified file in the window,
  across all editor groups, then reports how many it saved, how many it could not save, and how many untitled
  buffers it skipped. `File: Revert File` reads the file again from disk, asking first when that discards
  unsaved changes. The caret, scroll position and folds stay put, the file is read in the encoding chosen for
  it, and Local History keeps the discarded text. `Buffer: Reopen Closed Tab` brings back the file whose tab
  you closed last, with its caret where it was. It skips files deleted since and goes to a file that is
  already open again. All three are in the File menu. Keys: Save All is `Ctrl+K S` (VS Code; `⌥⌘S` on macOS)
  and `C-x s` (Emacs). Reopen Closed Tab is `Ctrl+Shift+T` in the VS Code, Sublime and CUA keymaps (`⇧⌘T` on
  macOS). To make room, the File menu's export formats moved into an Export submenu.
- **Choose a file's encoding.** Click the encoding in the status bar, or use `Buffer: Reopen with
  Encoding…` and `Buffer: Save with Encoding…` from the command palette. Reopening reads the file again in
  the encoding you pick — Shift_JIS, GBK, windows-1251 and about 40 other common ones are listed by script,
  then every encoding the runtime has — and remembers it for that file, including remote files. When the file
  is not valid in that encoding, nothing changes and the status line names the first line and column that
  could not be read. Saving with an encoding marks the tab modified until you save, wins over
  `.editorconfig`, and refuses a character the encoding cannot hold instead of switching to UTF-8. An
  encoding Editora could not detect is shown in the warning colour, with a tooltip that says so. The
  installed app now includes the JDK's extended charsets (ISO-2022-JP, the Hebrew, Arabic, Baltic and
  Vietnamese Windows code pages, MacRoman…), so the list is the same on every OS. File Information shows the
  file's real encoding instead of always UTF-8.
- **The Run, Output, Test Results, Debug and External Tools windows show a spinner while something runs.** A long
  script, build or test run that prints little or nothing no longer looks stalled: a small spinner beside the status turns
  from launch (including a run configuration's before-launch command) until it exits, is stopped, or fails to
  start. In Output, each tool's tab spins only for its own build, and a Git tab spins while a clone streams;
  the tab's title spins too, so a build in a tab you are not looking at still shows it is running.
  In Test Results it covers the compile step before the first test reports, when the progress bar is still empty.
  Debug spins while the before-launch build, the session start or the program runs, and stops at a breakpoint.
  An external tool that writes to the console now opens it at launch with the spinner, instead of only when it
  finishes; a tool that writes into the editor spins the External Tools header too. The Run window's stripe
  button also badges a small spinner on its icon while a program runs, so a run still shows it is alive with
  the Run window closed or another window open in its place.
- **Remote development is on, and set per host.** The tools Editora drives — Git, gh, ripgrep, builds, tests,
  language servers and debuggers — run on the host of a remote folder by default. The first time you open a
  folder on a host, Editora asks once whether it may run commands there. Settings → Remote now shows, for
  each saved site, whether that host may run commands (you can withdraw it there) and the command for each
  tool on that host when its PATH does not find the right one: Git, GitHub CLI, ripgrep, a JDK, Node.js,
  debugpy's Python, js-debug, java-debug, and any language server (`server = command`, one per line).
  Changes reach open windows at once. The global switch is in Settings → Remote and in the
  `Remote: Toggle Running Commands on the Host` command. Works with OpenSSH servers (on Linux and on macOS, where Remote Login is one) and dropbear: on a
  dropbear host, stopping a program also stops what it started, and a lost connection ends it, and on the
  older dropbear Debian 12 and Ubuntu 24.04 ship, a command no longer fails now and then with "the remote
  host did not start the command". Removing a
  saved site keeps that host's answer and tool commands, for when it is added back.
- **Tools in a container.** A project folder bind-mounted into a running container — the dev container that
  the Dev Containers CLI or VS Code started for it, or a container you pick with Containers: Run This
  Project's Tools in a Container… — can have its git, builds, tests, language servers and debuggers run
  inside the container, with the container's own PATH, environment and user, while you edit the files here.
  Editora asks once per container; Containers: Run This Project's Tools Here goes back. Works with Docker and
  Podman (Settings → Remote → Container engine). A debugger listening on a port inside the container is
  reached from here, whatever the container's network. Editora keeps its working files in `~/.cache/editora`
  inside the container, so the Java language server's index survives a restart, Debug works on a loose Java
  file and with the java-debug plugin Editora ships, and blame's ignore-revs settings work as on an SSH host.
- **Tools in WSL (Windows).** A project inside a WSL distribution, opened as `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\…`, can
  have its git, builds, tests, language servers and debuggers run inside that distribution with its own Linux
  tools, instead of Windows ones reading the files across the share. Editora asks once per distribution;
  Containers: Run This Project's Tools Here goes back. Changes made outside Editora (a `git pull` or a build
  in the distribution) now reach the Project tree, Git and the language servers: Windows cannot watch the
  share, so Editora watches the folder inside the distribution (with `inotifywait` when `inotify-tools` is
  installed, else by checking every few seconds).
- **Debugging in a container or WSL distribution built on Ubuntu 26.04 no longer hangs at "Connecting".** Such
  images (`eclipse-temurin:25` among them) ship the Rust coreutils, whose `cat` held the debug adapter's replies
  until the connection closed; Editora's relay to a port inside now copies with `dd`. Java debugging in a
  container is now tested end to end: jdtls and java-debug in the container, a breakpoint hit in a project's main
  class and in a loose Java file.
- **Programs left in a container by a crash are stopped.** A language server, debugger, build or run that
  Editora started in a container kept running there if Editora was killed, since ending Editora's side of the
  connection does not end it. The next launch now stops it, after checking it is still the same process. WSL
  distributions get the same check (WSL 1 already ends such programs along with Editora). On a normal quit,
  the last stop request is no longer lost to the exiting app.
- **Debugging in remote folders.** On a host you have allowed to run commands, Debug on a
  remote `.py` or `.js` file runs debugpy or vscode-js-debug on the file's host, with breakpoints, stepping and
  the call stack as for a local file. The host needs its own debugpy (`pip install debugpy`) or vscode-js-debug
  and node; their locations can be set per host. Breakpoints of a remote file are kept across reconnects.
  Java files in a Maven or Gradle project are debugged through the jdtls on the host (Debug, Debug Main
  Class, Attach, Debug Test and a saved configuration); Editora copies its java-debug plugin into
  `~/.cache/editora` there. A Java file outside a project is compiled on the host for the debugger too. A
  makefile at a remote project's root shows the run-configuration toolbar, as it does locally.
- **Language servers for remote folders.** On a host you have allowed to run commands, a file in a remote folder
  is served by a language server running on its host (pyright, gopls, rust-analyzer, the TypeScript server and
  the others), found on the host's PATH or configured per host: completion, hover, diagnostics, go to definition
  and the rest work as for local files. Renames and other cross-file edits create, move and delete files on the
  host, and checking such an edit before it lands no longer pauses the window for a round trip per file. A file outside the project on the same host (a library source reached by Go to Definition) is served by
  the project's server. Losing the connection stops the servers without reporting a crash, and reconnecting
  starts them again. Java works too: jdtls runs on the host with the host's JDKs and keeps its index in
  `~/.cache/editora` there (the host-consent question now says so).
- **Remote folders notice outside changes.** On a host you have allowed to run commands, a remote project's
  folder is watched on its host, so a `git pull` or a build there updates the Project tree, Git, language
  servers and an open file that changed, as for a local folder. Hosts with `inotifywait` report at once;
  others are checked every few seconds.
- **Run, builds and tests for remote folders.** On a host you have allowed to run commands, Run on a remote file,
  script / make / npm run configurations in a remote project, and Maven, Gradle, npm, Cargo and Go builds and
  test runs start on the host, over the same SSH connection; output, input and Stop work as for local runs.
  The host's own Java is used (or a JDK configured for that host). A Java project's main class — the gutter ▶,
  Run Main Class or a saved configuration — runs on the host too, with the class path its jdtls or Maven gives.
- **Find in Files and Go to File for remote folders.** On a host you have allowed to run commands, Find in Files
  in a remote (SFTP) folder is done by the host's own ripgrep when it has one, instead of reading every file
  over the connection, and Go to File lists a remote project's files on the host. Go to Symbol has no
  symbols for a remote project.
- **Git for remote folders.** On a host you have allowed to run commands,
  a repository on a remote (SFTP) host works as a local one does: branch, changed files, change bars, log and
  blame, and staging (whole files or single hunks), committing, branches, stashes and fetch / pull / push. It
  is the host's own `git`, over the same SSH connection, with the host's credentials. Editora asks once per host
  before running anything there. The GitHub tool window and commands use the host's own `gh` for such a
  repository, signed in there. Git: Clone in a remote project's window clones on that host, by its git, into a
  folder next to the project (typed as the host names it, `~` its home), and Git: Init creates a repository
  there. Fetch automatically fetches a remote repository on its host too, by the host's git, under the same
  rules as a local one (a trusted folder, or one you have fetched in yourself), leaving an ssh command the
  host's login profile exports alone. In a remote project that holds another repository (nested, a submodule,
  a worktree), the Project tree's Git actions on its files act on that repository, as they do locally. Blame
  of a remote file uses the repository's `.git-blame-ignore-revs`, and a `blame.ignoreRevsFile` in the host's
  global config that the repository lacks no longer stops blame there.
- **Remote folders are projects with their own window.** Connecting to a remote (SFTP) folder now opens it as
  a project in its own window, listed with your other projects, with its own tabs and trust. Reopening it later
  opens the window and asks to connect; while it is not connected the Project panel says so and offers
  Reconnect, and the tabs you had open come back when the connection does. A lost connection is shown the same
  way. The window you connected from is left as it was.
- **Markdown preview: text can be selected and copied.** Drag, double-click a word, triple-click a block,
  Shift-click, Shift+arrows and Select All work across paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, code blocks and alerts;
  Copy puts plain text and formatted HTML on the clipboard, and `Preview: Copy` copies the selection when there is
  one. Going to the source line is now a double-click beside the text, Ctrl/Cmd+double-click, or
  "Go to Source Line" in the preview's menu.
- **Markdown wiki links.** `[[note]]`, `[[note|label]]`, `[[note#heading]]` and `![[image.png]]` are links in the
  preview and in every export, resolve to the note beside the document or the one file of that name in the project,
  can be followed from the source and the preview, complete after `[[`, are rewritten when a note is renamed, and
  are checked by lint (`LINK003`). A **Backlinks** tool window (`Markdown: Show Backlinks`) lists what links to the
  current file. `Markdown: Convert Wiki Link` turns one into a Markdown link and back. A setting switches wiki
  links off.
- **Remote images can be asked for per document.** The remote-images setting is now Always / Ask / Never; with Ask,
  nothing is fetched when a document opens and a bar in the preview offers to load its remote images.
- **Markdown link updates on rename** now use a link index kept while the project is open, also rewrite HTML
  `src` / `href` paths and wiki links, record a Local History entry before changing a file that is not open, and
  change a file open in another window through that window (one undo step) instead of on disk.
- **PDF export** draws highlight, superscript and subscript, and emoji with a bundled monochrome emoji font (Noto
  Emoji). Alerts are coloured and titled and definition lists indented in PDF, Word and OpenDocument exports.
  Highlighted code in exported HTML follows the page's light or dark scheme.
- **Markdown source:** the text line of a setext heading is styled as a heading, ticked and open task boxes are
  told apart, and bare URLs are styled as links.
- **Unused pasted images are cleaned up.** When a document is saved, an image pasted or dropped in this session
  that the document no longer mentions is moved to the trash (a setting, on by default); the check and the move
  run in the background.
- **Command palette:** a command is also found by the first part of its id, so "markdown table" finds the
  `Table: …` commands.
- Smaller Markdown additions: an image or diagram in the preview can be enlarged from the keyboard and the menu;
  hidden front matter is also left out of print; the default view applies to untitled Markdown buffers; ordered
  lists are renumbered after deleting or cutting and pasting whole items; Paste as Markdown handles merged cells,
  nested tables and definition lists; links in the completion documentation popup can be followed;
  "Disable for This Project" can edit YAML and `.markdownlint-cli2` configs; a changed `.markdownlint` file outside
  a project is noticed when the window regains focus.
- **Markdown: more syntax, in the preview and in every export.** GitHub alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`,
  `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!CAUTION]`), emoji shortcodes (`:rocket:`), `==highlight==`, `^superscript^` and
  `~subscript~`, definition lists, ```` ```math ```` fences and `\(…\)` / `\[…\]` math. In the preview: task
  checkboxes can be clicked to tick the source, a double-click on a block puts the caret on its source line, the
  block holding the caret is marked in Split, code blocks show their language, an image or diagram enlarges on
  click, front matter is a table (and can be hidden), and an empty document says so.
- **Markdown preview to the side or in its own tab** (`Markdown: Open Preview to the Side`, `Markdown: Open Preview
  in a Tab`), following the active Markdown file or locked to one.
- **Markdown completion:** relative paths after `](`, heading anchors after `#` (this file and `file.md#`),
  reference labels, emoji after `:`, languages after a fence, and Mermaid keywords inside a Mermaid fence.
- **Markdown links follow a renamed or moved file.** Renaming or moving a file in the project offers to update the
  Markdown links that point to it, and a moved document's own relative links; the setting chooses ask (default),
  always or never.
- **Markdown navigation:** the breadcrumb shows the path of headings at the caret, and
  `Project: Go to Markdown Heading…` searches the headings of every Markdown file in the project.
- **Markdown editing commands:** numbered list, block quote and code block toggles, Toggle Task Done, Renumber List,
  Insert Footnote, Insert Date, Insert Horizontal Rule and Insert Image…; table tools to move a row or column, sort
  by a column, insert a row above or a column to the left, and delete the table; link tools to edit a link, remove
  it, or convert between inline and reference links; `Markdown: Paste as Markdown` turns copied HTML or spreadsheet
  cells into Markdown, and an ordinary paste does the same for HTML that holds a table, link, list or heading. Tab
  and Shift-Tab move a list item with its children; `*` and `_` are paired like other markers.
- **Markdown: Format Document / Format Selection** normalises list markers and numbering, emphasis style, heading
  style, blank lines around blocks, table alignment and trailing whitespace, leaving code, front matter and HTML
  alone. `Markdown: Number Headings` and `Remove Heading Numbers` add, update and remove section numbers.
- **Markdown lint: 29 more rules** — MD003, MD004, MD005, MD007, MD011, MD013, MD024, MD029, MD030, MD032, MD033,
  MD035, MD036, MD037, MD038, MD039, MD042, MD045, MD046, MD048, MD049, MD050, MD051, MD053, MD055, MD056, MD058, and
  two of Editora's own: `LINK001` (a relative link or image whose file does not exist) and `LINK002` (a link to a
  heading that is not in the linked file). Eleven have fixes. MD013 (line length) and MD033 (inline HTML) are off
  until enabled; MD024 flags repeated headings among siblings only. Also new: a severity per rule (error, warning,
  hint), Fix on Save, Fix Issues in Selection, Disable for This File / This Project, `Markdown Lint: Lint Project`
  with results grouped by file, an issue count in the status bar, and open files are re-linted when a
  `.markdownlint` file changes.
- **Markdown settings:** default view for Markdown files, preview font size and column width, scroll sync, hide
  front matter, smart typography (curly quotes, dashes, ellipsis), table-of-contents options (skip the title,
  numbered, update on save), name pattern and alt-text prompt for pasted images, lint fix-on-save and severities,
  link updates on rename, and for HTML export: embed images and highlight code (both on).
- **Status bar word count** for Markdown and plain text, with the selection's count and reading time; **typewriter
  mode** keeps the caret line centred while typing. Lists and block quotes fold.
- **Exported HTML is self-contained:** local images are embedded, code blocks are highlighted, and Mermaid diagrams
  are drawn when the Mermaid CLI is available.
- **Markdown: links inside a document can be followed.** `Markdown: Open Link`, Ctrl/Cmd-click and a click in the
  preview now follow `#heading`, `other.md#heading` and reference links (`[text][label]`); the jump is recorded, so
  Back returns to the link. The table of contents Editora generates is navigable. Link destinations with
  parentheses or in `<…>` form are read correctly.
- **Markdown lint: act on an issue.** Next / Previous Issue, Fix This Issue, Disable for This Line, Disable Rule and
  Open Rule Documentation, from the palette, the editor's right-click menu and the Lint tool window (which gained a
  Fix button, a row menu with Copy, and the file name). Fix Issues reports how many issues it fixed and how many
  need manual changes. Project configs are read as markdownlint reads them: comments, YAML, `.markdownlint-cli2`
  files, rule aliases and tags, `extends`, and the options of the rules Editora implements; a rule the project
  switches on wins over the global "off". Directives `disable-file`, `enable-file`, `capture`, `restore` and
  `configure-file` are honoured. Bare e-mail addresses are reported under MD034.
- **Markdown preview:** Find searches the rendered preview when only the preview is showing. A safe subset of HTML
  is rendered (`<br>`, `<kbd>`, `<sub>`/`<sup>`, `<b>`/`<i>`/`<em>`/`<strong>`/`<code>`, `<a>`, `<img>`,
  `<details>`/`<summary>`, `align="center"`). Footnotes are numbered and linked both ways, inline footnotes
  (`^[…]`) are recognised, the right-click menu has Copy Code Block on a code block and Copy Link Address on a link, and links can be reached with Tab.
  The light/dark toggle can return to "follow the app theme"; zoom and the Split divider are remembered per file.
- **Markdown settings:** load remote images (on by default), preview theme (Follows the app theme / Light / Dark),
  folder for pasted images, and the heading levels listed by the table of contents.
- **Markdown editing:** Tab / Shift-Tab indent and outdent a list item; Enter on an empty nested item steps out one
  level; Enter on an empty last table row leaves the table; an ordered list is renumbered after Enter or a moved
  line; bold/italic with no selection toggle the word under the caret; typing `*`, `_` or `~` over a selection wraps
  it. The table-size picker works from the keyboard and opens at the caret. The format bar shows the current
  heading level and which styles are active, and names each command's key binding when the keymap has one.
- **Exports:** Word documents get real heading styles, numbered and bulleted lists, table alignment, inline images,
  internal links for `#heading` and a document title; OpenDocument gets table alignment. `.mdx`, `.Rmd`, `.qmd`,
  `.mdwn` and `.mkdn` open as Markdown.
- **`LSP: Clear Java Index Caches` frees the disk space the Java language server used.** It keeps an index per
  Java folder you have opened (in `~/.editora/jdtls-workspaces`, about 40 MB each and often far more), and nothing
  ever removed one. The command deletes every index that no running server is using and reports the space freed;
  jdtls rebuilds a project's index the next time it opens.
- **Abbreviations show what they expand to.** With abbrev-mode on, an abbreviation typed out in full shows its
  expansion as muted text after the caret (`btw → by the way`), as a snippet trigger does. Tab expands it now,
  Escape hides the hint, and typing on expands it as before.

### Changed

- **Run configurations belong to projects.** The No Project window has no run-configuration selector, Run or
  Debug buttons, and its Save, Edit, Delete and Run/Debug Configuration commands say to open a project. There
  you run a script or a compact Java file from its gutter ▶ or with Run File. A Maven or Gradle checkout opened
  as loose files no longer shows the toolbar group either. Configurations the global session saved before are
  kept in its state, not deleted; they are just not offered.
- **Without a project, the TODO window lists only the current tab.** It is hidden, stripe button included,
  while that tab has no TODOs, and comes back by itself on a tab or edit that has some if it was open when it
  was hidden. It follows edits as you type. Project windows still scan the whole project.
- **Go to Definition works without a language server.** When LSP is off, no server handles the file, or the
  server finds nothing, it looks the name up in this file and then in the project's symbol index.
- **The Run console draws colours** (ANSI codes become theme colours), a `\r` progress bar stays on one line,
  and a clear-screen code clears it. Shell runs get `TERM=xterm-256color` unless the configuration sets one.
- **Stop says "Stopped"** instead of "Process finished with exit code 143".
- **Shell snippets follow the shebang:** `if`, `elif`, `while` and `until` use `[ ]` in `#!/bin/sh` and dash
  scripts. New triggers `elif` and `arith` (`$(( … ))`); `elseif` and `expr` still work. Loops and `function`
  are laid out the usual way and no snippet adds a blank line after itself.
- **File templates follow `.editorconfig` `indent_style` and `indent_size`.** New ▸ Zsh starts with the same strict
  preamble as the Zsh Script template.
- **Run Configurations suits scripts:** Add proposes the open shell or Python script, Save as Run Configuration
  saves script configurations, Script / target has a Browse button, rows a type does not use are hidden, and
  labels are no longer cut off.
- **Language-server status messages name their server** ("bash-language-server: Analyzing workspace") instead of
  always saying "Java LSP".
- **Outlines from servers that send a flat symbol list** (bash-language-server among them) are nested under their
  functions, and a variable assigned twice is listed once.
- **Hints are drawn fainter than information**, and code a server marks as unused is faded.
- **Shell scripts run with default settings.** The gutter ▶, Run File and the Run button used to appear for a
  shell script only when LSP support and the Bash server were both switched on, so a new user could not run
  one at all. Shell Run now works like Python Run, for local and remote files.
- **Run uses the interpreter the shebang names, with its flags.** It used to run every shell script with
  `bash`: a `#!/bin/sh` script ran under bash, a `.zsh` file ran under bash, and a `-e` or `-u` in the
  shebang was dropped, so a script relying on `-e` kept going after a failing step. `#!/usr/bin/env -S bash -e`
  works. With no shebang, `.zsh` files run with `zsh` and other shell files with `bash`.
- **Program arguments and environment variables are read like a shell reads them.** Backslash escapes work
  (`tail\ x`, `"say \"hi\""`), an unclosed quote is reported instead of silently swallowing the rest of the
  line, and environment values expand `$NAME` and `${NAME}` (`PATH=/opt/x/bin:$PATH`). This applies to Run,
  run configurations and Debug.
- **A relative working directory in a run configuration is relative to the project**, or to the script's
  folder when there is no project, never to the folder Editora was started from. A missing directory or
  script is named in the error.
- **`;;` in a shell `case` statement is typed at the body's level**, as shfmt and Google's style guide place
  it, and the bundled `case` snippet matches.
- **Shell command arguments and options are plain text**, no longer string-coloured or spell-checked, so
  `set -euo pipefail` or `apt-get install libssl-dev` no longer gets red squiggles. Quoted strings, comments
  and here-doc text are still checked.
- **Shell scripts keep LF line endings and no byte-order mark** even when `.editorconfig` asks for CRLF or
  `utf-8-bom`; new shell files from New ▸ and templates are written that way.
- **Format Document sends the file's own indentation** (from `.editorconfig` or what the file uses) to the
  language server instead of the global tab size, so shfmt no longer re-indents a 2-space script to 4.
- **Recent Files dropdown fits its names and asks before removing one.** The dropdown is as wide as the
  longest file name, up to a limit, so names are no longer cut short. The project labels line up in one
  column. Clicking a row's trash icon now asks before removing that file from the list, and the question
  shows the full path, so two files with the same name are easy to tell apart.
- **HTTP Client: what a request sends is closer to the JetBrains format.** Lines starting with `#` or `//`
  inside a request body are comments and are no longer sent (shell or Markdown bodies that need such lines can
  go in a `< ./file`). Directives (`# @no-redirect`, `# @timeout`) count only above the request line, and
  `@timeout` / `@connection-timeout` take units (`500 ms`, `5 s`, `2 m`). An `@var` line applies to the requests
  below it, so a later one can redefine it. `http://` requests go out as HTTP/1.1, without the `Upgrade: h2c`
  headers the JDK used to add, and `HTTP/1.1` or `HTTP/2` on the request line is honoured. `>>` onto a file that
  exists writes `name-1.json`, `name-2.json`, … instead of skipping the save, and `>>` paths take `{{variables}}`.
  GraphQL, WebSocket and gRPC requests are reported as not supported instead of being sent as broken GETs.
- **HTTP Client: the response view shows what happened.** The top line reads `404 Not Found · 12 ms · 4 B`,
  coloured by outcome, with the protocol version above the headers and a "Request" section showing the request as
  sent, variables filled in. A running request shows its elapsed time, Run All shows "2 of 5: GET …" and lands
  on the first failure with a "3 of 13 failed" summary, and one Run / Cancel button re-sends the request the
  selected response came from, even after the file was edited: a named response runs only the request of that
  name, an unnamed one the request with the same text or URL; when it is gone, the request at the caret runs and
  the panel says so. Warnings have their own block with a count beside the status line, and the warnings and
  headers get the room their text needs. A request that was never sent reads "Not sent", and Copy as cURL is off
  for it. Cancelling a Run All keeps the responses that had already arrived and says how many ran; History lists
  a Run All's responses newest first. The toolbar wraps instead of shrinking to "…". Long lines can be wrapped,
  one-line XML is indented, and images are shown as pictures.
- **HTTP Client: history and environments are remembered per file.** The last 10 responses of each `.http` file,
  and its environment, are kept in Editora's config folder and come back when the file is reopened. Bodies are
  capped at 1 MB; credential headers (Authorization, cookies, API keys, tokens, passwords) and every value a
  request read from an environment variable or `.env` are masked, in the saved file and in History; requests
  marked `# @no-log` are never saved. A restored response still knows how its request was sent, so Copy as cURL
  after a restart reproduces the upload, form or Digest login. Two windows on one file keep each other's
  responses, the history follows a file renamed or moved (also from the Project tree) and is removed with a
  deleted one, a Run pressed right after opening a file no longer wipes the saved responses, and Export
  Configuration includes it only when you tick "Include HTTP response history". Environment files are found in
  the file's folder or the nearest folder above it, up to the open project's root, else the file's repository
  root; outside a repository only the file's own folder counts. Environments defined only in
  `http-client.private.env.json` are listed. Env files may hold comments, trailing commas or a byte-order mark;
  one that cannot be read is named in the run's warnings and in the underline's tooltip, numbers are sent as
  written, and an env file edited in another program is picked up when the window regains focus. A
  chained request (`{{login.response.body.$.token}}`) works when requests are run one at a time; the session is
  cleared when the environment changes.
- **HTTP Client: keyboard and editor.** Run Request at Caret is bound to `C-c C-c` (Emacs) and `Ctrl+Alt+R`
  (VS Code, CUA, Sublime, IntelliJ), Run All Requests to `C-c C-r` (Emacs) and `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Enter`
  (`Option+Cmd+Shift+Enter` on macOS; GNOME keeps `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+R` for screen recording), and Cancel to
  `C-c C-k` (Emacs) and `Ctrl+Alt+K` (`Option+Cmd+K` on macOS; the IntelliJ keymap on macOS keeps Control+Option);
  the ▶ tooltip names both run chords. While a request runs its ▶ turns into a ■ that cancels it (a folded
  request keeps its ▶ or ■ on its `###` line), and the "Running …" line shows the request with its variables
  filled in. Escape in the response view returns to the editor, and the response view takes the keymap's motion
  and copy keys (Emacs `M-w`, `C-n`, `M->`). Run File and the editor's context menu run the file's requests. `.http` files get request
  folding, one Structure entry per request, completion for methods and headers, a starter request in New File,
  and richer highlighting (variables, directives, JSON and XML bodies, file references, scripts).
- **HTTP Client: unresolved variables are underlined as you type.** A `{{variable}}` that cannot resolve with the
  selected environment, the `@var` lines above it and the built-ins gets a warning underline; hover for the
  reason; with no environment selected, it names the environments that define the variable. Typing `{{` offers
  the variables available there (a nested environment member one level at a time), the dynamic built-ins, `.env`
  keys and `name.response.` for each request in the file. `\{{` stands for a literal `{{`.
- **HTTP Client: requests from remote files don't run yet.** On a file opened from a remote folder, Run, Run All
  and Cancel say so instead of sending the request from this machine, and the response view's Run is disabled
  with a tooltip saying why.
- **HTTP Client: an untitled `.http` file can send requests.** It uses the project's environment files, and its
  responses are kept when you save it. A request that needs the file's folder (a body file, a `>>` target,
  `$dotenv`) is not sent and says to save the file first.
- **HTTP Client: Save response writes the body exactly as received** (an image saves as the image), named after
  the URL, in the request's folder. The status-and-headers text report is the second choice in the dialog.
- **The installed Linux app is 22 MB smaller.** The bundled Java runtime no longer carries the unused client and minimal
  JVMs beside the server one.
- **Snippet words no longer expand in the middle of a sentence.** In a Markdown or plain-text document, Tab after a word such
  as `code`, `link` or `bold` expands the snippet only when the word is alone on its line or is chosen from the
  completion popup.
- **A double-click in the Markdown preview selects the word** instead of jumping to the source line (see the
  preview selection entry above for the new ways to go to the source).
- **The remote-images setting** is now a choice (Always / Ask / Never); a stored "off" becomes Never.
  `View: Toggle Markdown Remote Images` switches between Always and Never.
- **A single tilde pair attached to the word before it is a subscript** in the Markdown preview (`H~2~O`); standing
  apart, `~struck~` is still strikethrough, as is `~~struck~~`. An ordinary paste of copied HTML that holds a table, link, list or heading arrives as
  Markdown. Exported HTML no longer accepts `data:` URIs as link targets, and as image sources only `data:image/`.
- **Word wrap is now set per kind of file: on for Markdown and plain text, off for code.** "Wrap long lines in code"
  keeps the old setting; a new "Wrap long lines in Markdown and plain text" governs them. If you had switched word
  wrap on, everything still wraps. Toggle Word Wrap flips the preference that governs the file in front. A buffer
  with a very long unbroken run of characters opens unwrapped until toggled.
- **A buffer showing only the Markdown preview refuses editing commands** (with a status message) instead of
  editing the hidden source; switch to Editor or Split to edit.
- **Markdown preview:** entering Preview opens at the editor's position, and Split keeps the two panes on the same
  block instead of the same scroll fraction. Code blocks and wide tables scroll sideways instead of wrapping or
  being squeezed. The preview menu's "Select All" selects the preview's text instead of copying the document, "Copy" copies
  the selection, and the old "Copy" (the whole document) is "Copy All".
- **Markdown lint:** a front-matter `title:` counts as the document's top-level heading (as in markdownlint); the
  search for `.markdownlint.*` stops at the project or Git root; with the minimap visible the scrollbar lint stripe
  is hidden, since the minimap shows the same marks.
- **Markdown editing commands** keep the caret where it was instead of selecting the changed lines; promoting an H1
  leaves it an H1; a heading command on a list or quote line puts the heading behind the marker; with several
  carets a Markdown command collapses to one and says so. When the clipboard holds both a picture and text, paste
  inserts the text. Pasted images get the file's name as alt text, and an image dropped from under the document's
  own folder is linked in place instead of copied.
- **Export command titles** are now "File: Export Preview to PDF… / Word (.docx)… / OpenDocument (.odt)… / HTML…";
  OpenDocument export is in the File menu. The HTML and office document title comes from the front matter's
  `title:`, then the first heading, then the file name. Exported HTML follows the reader's light/dark preference.

### Security

- **An `.http` file can no longer send your environment secrets without asking.** A request that reads
  `$processEnv`, `$env` or `$dotenv` from a folder you have not trusted now asks first, whatever form the read
  takes: `{{$env NAME}}` or `{{$env.NAME}}`, through an `@var` line or an environment value, in a header, a `<@`
  body file or a multipart `<@` part. The check follows what the request actually resolves, so no spelling slips
  past it. The prompt names the variables as written, never their values, and the hosts the request goes to (a
  redirect may lead elsewhere); declining sends none of the requests that read a secret (in a Run All the others
  still go), and a refused secret is never shown or saved. A request that is never sent (GraphQL, a missing body
  file) asks nothing and shows or saves no secret; a host chosen by an earlier response is named as such; Enter
  in the prompt cancels it. `.env` is read only when it is a regular file inside the folder, up to 1 MB. It uses
  the same trust as build scripts, so a trusted project is asked once, and the check runs off the UI thread, so a
  malformed `{{` cannot freeze the window. Before, a request in a cloned repository could send, say,
  `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` to any host on one click.
- **HTTP Client: Copy as cURL is safe to paste into bash or zsh.** The URL and header names were put in the shell command
  unquoted, so a crafted URL ran commands when the copied cURL was pasted into a terminal, and a body starting
  with `@` made curl upload a local file. Every word is quoted now, and the command reproduces what was sent:
  `--data-binary @file` for file bodies, `-F` for forms (with their parts' types and file names), `--digest`,
  `-L` and the HTTP version (`--http1.0` and `--http2-prior-knowledge` too). A redirected POST turns into a GET
  as it did in the run, and no `Content-Type` is added that was not sent. Import cURL writes an imported `{{` as
  `\{{`, so text from a copied command never turns into a variable, and says when it did.

### Fixed

- **Java scripts get Java editing.** A file without the `.java` name that is Java — an extensionless
  `#!/usr/bin/env -S java --source 25` script, or a file set to Java in the status bar — now gets completion
  (with imports, added below the shebang line), hover, the outline and syntax errors from
  jdtls. jdtls works only on files named `.java`, so it used to ignore such a script, and its test-gutter check
  logged a stack trace in the Debug Log on every switch to the tab. Like any `.java` file outside a project, it
  gets syntax errors only, not type errors. Debugging such a script is unchanged.
- **Highlights and markers drawn over the text no longer lag the text by a frame.** Find matches, symbol
  occurrences, whitespace markers, TODO highlights, spelling and LSP squiggles, Markdown and Mermaid lint, log
  levels, inline debug values, snippet fields and AceJump labels are painted after the text is laid out, like
  the Personal Notes indicators and the indent guides. When the line numbers gained a digit at the 1,000th line,
  or were toggled, one frame showed them where the text had been (8 px off in a headless probe).
- **Personal Notes indicators stay on the note's text, and cost less.**
  - The highlight and its corner marker are painted after the text is laid out, so they no longer sit where the
    text was for a frame (or more) when the line numbers gain a digit or are toggled, or the font changes.
  - A note that runs onto the next row of a wrapped line paints only its own text on each row, not both rows in
    full. A note on a folded line is not painted, and scrolled sideways no highlight covers the line numbers.
  - Typing in a file with notes no longer rebuilds the gutter of each note's line: an Enter above 200 notes
    queued 400 gutter rebuilds (41 s of work in a headless probe, now 0.1 s). Opening a file and turning the
    indicators on or off no longer rebuild the whole gutter either (12 ms to 1.5 ms per open).
  - Opening a file while you have notes on other files no longer reads and hashes the whole file (up to 5 MB) to
    look for a renamed file's notes; it is hashed only when a note's file is gone and had the same size.
  - Moving the pointer over a buffer without notes no longer hit-tests it, and a click checks only the markers on
    screen.
- **HTTP Client: a failing pre-request script is named as one.** Its Tests block read "Response handler error"
  and its badge "✗ handler error"; they now say "Pre-request script error" and "✗ pre-request error". A Tests
  block with only log lines is titled "Script output", since either kind of script may have written them, and a
  script that runs out of time "did not finish", not "the handler did not finish".
- **HTTP Client: a `{{name}}` set by a script file is not underlined.** A name a `< ./pre.js` or `> ./check.js`
  file sets with `request.variables.set` or `client.global.set` was marked as unresolved, because only inline
  scripts were read. The check now reads the script files a `.http` file names (as a run finds them, up to
  1 MB; reading one to find names runs nothing). An edit to a script file shows on the next check of the
  `.http` file.
- **Export Configuration leaves out the installed ShellCheck and shfmt** (`plugins/tools/`) and the Typst CLI
  (`plugins/typst/`), as it already did language servers and debug adapters. The zip no longer carries about
  20 MB of executables built for this machine's OS. A plugin can no longer take the id `tools`, so installing or
  removing one cannot overwrite or delete those tools.
- **Startup files have no Run ▶:** `.bashrc`, `.profile`, `.zshrc`, `.xinitrc`, `.bash_logout`, `.envrc` and
  the other rc, profile, login and session files. One stray click no longer runs them.
- **Debug on a shell script says it cannot be debugged** and points to Run with Trace, instead of sending you to
  Settings. An untitled buffer no debugger handles is told so before any Save As prompt.
- **Bash and dash error lines in the Run console are links** (`deploy.sh: line 12: …`).
- **Rerun and run configurations save the script they run**, not whichever tab is in front.
- **Shebangs with `env -u NAME`, `env -C DIR`, `-Sbash`, `--split-string=…` or `#!/bin/busybox sh`** are recognised
  and run correctly.
- **More shell files are recognised:** `.bats`, `.command` and bash-completion scripts.
- **Shell highlighting:** `$?` and `$#` look like other variables; `${x:+y}`, `${x^^}` and `${x,,}` operators are
  coloured; the command in `${x:-$(cmd)}` and the regex after `=~` are coloured; `&>` is a redirection;
  `for i in {1..10}`, `select … in` and `coproc` are right; zsh `{ cmd }` groups close. Function bodies now
  highlight as in VS Code, which also tidies C++, GraphQL, Groovy and Markdown.
- **Tab icons follow the file's detected language**, for shebang scripts and languages picked in the status bar.
- **The symbol index for shell** finds `pkg::fn` and `lib.fn` functions and top-level `readonly`/`declare`/`export`
  variables, ignores text inside here-docs and multi-line strings, and indexes extension-less `#!` scripts.
- **Double-click in a shell script selects `--long-flag`, `a-b.sh` or `my-func` whole.**
- **Toggle Comment leaves here-doc text alone** when a selection reaches into a here-doc without its first line.
- **A script whose workspace is the home folder, the temp folder or a filesystem root** (`~/.bashrc`, `/tmp/x.sh`)
  no longer makes bash-language-server scan that whole tree.
- **Shell scripts are opened on the language server as `shellscript`**, the standard language id.
- **Creating a script where the executable bit cannot be set** (Windows, FAT drives) now says so and how to fix it.
- **Shell highlighting no longer runs to the end of the file** after `$((x << 2))` or a `<<\EOF` here-doc.
  `$(( … ))` is now coloured as arithmetic. Two tests now guard the bundled grammars.
- **More files are recognised as shell scripts, everywhere at once:** `.envrc`, `/etc/bashrc`, `/etc/zshrc`
  and the other system zsh files, `/etc/profile`, `.ksh`, `*.bashrc`, `*.profile` (so `/etc/bash.bashrc`),
  `.mkshrc`, `PKGBUILD`, `APKBUILD`, `.ebuild` and `.eclass`. Some used to open as INI, where every `;` started a
  comment; others were coloured as shell but had no comment toggling, Run or language server.
- **A language picked in the status bar, or a shebang typed into a new file, reaches the language server and
  Run straight away**, and the status bar shows it. Before, only the colours changed.
- **zsh startup files (`.zshrc`, `.zprofile`, `/etc/zsh/zshenv` …) are no longer checked as bash**, which showed
  false errors on valid zsh.
- **`case` patterns no longer upset bracket-pair colours** (the pattern's `)` showed as unmatched and threw
  off the enclosing function's braces).
- **Typing shell code indents correctly:** the body of a `case` item is indented under its pattern, `esac`,
  `fi` and `done` line up with the line that opened them, and a here-doc's closing delimiter is no longer
  indented (bash did not recognise it, so the rest of the script became here-doc text). Nothing re-indents
  inside a here-doc, and `done=false` is no longer taken for `done`.
- **Toggle Comment never comments out or breaks a script's `#!` line.**
- **A `# region` marker no longer empties the Structure panel** for shell, Python, Ruby and other languages
  without block folding.
- **Enter after `else` or `break` in a shell script types a new line** instead of expanding the snippet of the
  same name. Tab still expands it.
- **Long hovers scroll.** A man page shown for a shell command made a popup thousands of pixels tall; the
  popup is now capped at about half the window and scrolls.
- **The status bar's LSP segment and the Problems button appear as soon as a file is opened on a server**,
  not only after switching tabs.
- **`read -p` prompts show in the Run console.** Bash prints them only to a terminal, so a script waiting for
  an answer showed nothing.
- **Windows: Run finds Git Bash** and no longer picks WSL's `bash.exe`, which cannot open a Windows path.
  Typed input reaches a shell with Unix line endings.
- **Personal Notes colours match Bookmarks.** Project headers in the Personal Notes tree are accent-coloured
  again and file headers are muted, as in Bookmarks. The two panels now share one set of style rules.
- **Java completions show the whole signature.** The completion list now grows to 1100 px instead of 760 px, so
  long method signatures such as `Files.find(…)` or `Map.merge(…)` are no longer cut off. It still sizes itself to
  the widest row, so short lists stay narrow.
- **A program written a moment ago no longer fails to start with "Text file busy".** On Linux, running a script
  you had just saved could fail when Editora happened to be starting another process while the file was being
  written. The Run tool window then showed `error: 26 (Text file busy)`, and the Doctor and the tool checks
  reported such a program as not installed. The same could stop a build through a wrapper script that had just
  changed (`./gradlew`, `./mvnw`), or a language server, debug adapter or AI agent that had just been installed.
  Editora now waits briefly and tries again.
- **Tabs keep their theme colours when the minimap redraws.** Redrawing the minimap made JavaFX restyle the
  whole window outside its normal frame. Just after a tab was opened or marked modified, that restyle could fail
  to find the theme's colours: the debug log filled with `Could not resolve '-color-fg-default'` warnings, and
  the selected tab's title could stay black instead of the theme's colour until something restyled it again.
  The minimap now draws off screen and leaves the window alone. A redraw also costs less, roughly a third as
  much when the window has pending style changes.
- **A language server that fails to start no longer leaves its tabs looking served.** When a server could not be
  started (its command cannot be run, or a remote connection broke while it was starting), its tabs stayed marked
  as served and the status bar could keep naming it until the tab was synced again. They now go quiet at once,
  as after a lost connection, and the server is not restarted in a loop. While Editora was finding out which
  servers are installed, such a server was also tried again once for every other server it checked (up to 22
  failed starts at launch); now only its own check, a settings change, Restart Servers or a reconnect tries
  it again.
- **Right-click menus close when you click outside them.** A click anywhere else in the tree, list, editor or
  panel the menu was opened on used to leave it open, and right-clicking another row opened a second menu
  beside the first. Now any click outside a right-click menu closes it, in every panel, and the click still
  does what it would have done (selects the row, moves the caret, opens that row's menu).
- **The window moves when you drag its title.** With the menu bar merged into the title bar, dragging the file
  name in the middle did nothing; only the empty parts of the bar moved the window.
- **HTTP Client: timestamps are right outside UTC.** `$timestamp`, `$isoTimestamp` and `$datetime iso8601`
  were off by the local UTC offset (six hours early in Mexico City). Day.js formats (`"DD-MM-YYYY"`) no longer
  give wrong dates, and `$env.NAME` and `{{$randomInt 1 10}}` work.
- **HTTP Client: nothing goes out silently wrong.** A `{{variable}}` that cannot be resolved (a typo, no
  environment selected, an earlier request not run yet, a missing `.env` key) is still sent empty but is now
  named in the response's warnings, as are skipped JetBrains `> {% %}` / `< {% %}` scripts. A pre-request script
  above a request no longer turns into the request line. `{{$dotenv X}}` works in `@var` lines.
- **HTTP Client: a request that fails unexpectedly reports it.** An internal error or running out of memory left
  the view on "Running…" for good and dropped the rest of a Run All; it now shows as that request's failure.
  The response history keeps at most 100 MB of bodies per file.
- **HTTP Client: large multipart uploads are streamed from disk** instead of read into memory, also for Digest
  `auth-int`, and Copy as cURL fills in variables in multipart file paths.
- **HTTP Client: responses and requests are byte-correct.** gzip and deflate responses are decoded (a browser's
  "Copy as cURL" with `accept-encoding` showed garbage), the charset of an HTML `<meta>` or XML prolog is used, and
  octet-stream, images, PDFs and archives count as binary. Request bodies use the charset `Content-Type` declares.
  Emoji in URLs are encoded correctly, a stray `%` is escaped, and non-ASCII host names work. Multipart parts fill
  in variables and lose the stray trailing newline.
- **HTTP Client: more requests work.** `GET /path` with a `Host:` header, a custom `Host`, lowercase and custom
  methods (`PROPFIND`, `QUERY`), a URL without `http://`, indented headers, and the caret on a request's `###`,
  `# @name` or directive line. Digest answers SHA-256 and other RFC 7616 challenges, and Basic/Digest shorthand
  passwords may contain spaces. `@timeout` also stops a body that stalls. Import cURL handles browser and Windows
  copies (Chrome's cmd copies with multi-line bodies included), `curl.exe`, `$ curl` and `/usr/bin/curl`, `-F`
  with typed parts, `--json`, `-d @file`, `-G`, `-I`, `--url-query`, `-H 'Name:'`, `--http2-prior-knowledge` and
  options with arguments, works outside a `.http` file, and warns when body lines would be read as comments or
  scripts.
- **HTTP Client: smaller fixes.** `$datetime` writes full month and weekday names (`MMMM`, `dddd`), Day.js
  formats such as `Do`, `Q`, `d`, `[W]ww` and `GGGG` come out right, a letter Day.js does not format (outside
  `[brackets]`) is reported instead of being sent as text, and a huge date offset gives a warning instead of an
  error. `< ./body-{{v}}.json` paths take variables, and an infinite `$random.float` range is reported. Indented (YAML) bodies keep their first line's indentation. A nested environment object merges across
  both env files, and `.env` accepts `export<TAB>` and multi-line quoted values. Copy as cURL of a multipart
  upload imports back, and curl import keeps `--http1.1` / `--http2` and turns `-T file` into a PUT. More
  credential headers are masked in the saved history (`X-Auth-Key`, `…-Key`, session and signature headers).
  Cancelling an upload releases the file at once, and a cancelled re-run of a login no longer empties the token
  later requests use. Messages about headers, body files, `>>` saves and stalled responses are translated, the
  elapsed time uses your language's decimal separator, and Escape in Preview goes back to the editor. `@var`
  lines fold with their request, browser multipart boundaries are coloured, and a Save As from `.http` to `.md`
  swaps the variable underlines for Markdown lint.
- **HTTP Client: saved responses are not lost, and Run on one sends the right request.** A Clear keeps a
  response that arrives after it, quitting waits for the last save, and a damaged entry is kept in a
  `.corrupt.bak` copy that the message names. Run on a History entry no longer freezes on a long URL, and a
  single cancelled request whose answer had already arrived says so.
- **HTTP Client: no file work on the UI thread.** Environment files are read in the background (and by the run
  itself as it starts, so it sends what they hold then), and Save response writes in the background, so a slow
  disk or a 50 MB response no longer holds up the window.
- **HTTP Client: clearer messages.** "Connection refused — is a server listening on …?", "Host not found",
  untrusted certificates and timeouts read as sentences instead of `ConnectException`; failures no longer read
  "exit 404" or "exit 5". A redirect to another host names the custom headers that went along, and a redirect
  loop or an HTTPS→HTTP redirect says why it stopped. Environment merging follows JetBrains (a private `$shared`
  value no longer beats a public environment's), nested environment objects are reachable as `{{a.b}}`, and an
  environment value may refer to another. Run File on a `.http` file no longer launches `java api.http`, and the
  "feature disabled" message names the right Settings page. Remote `.http` files no longer regain the ▶ after a
  settings change.
- **Stopping a debug session can no longer hold the window on a debugger connection that is slow to close.**
  The connection is half-closed first, so the adapter ends it, and the close itself no longer runs on the
  thread that pressed Stop. A close that never returned held two test runs on macOS for half an hour.
- **Remote commands get what the account's login profile sets.** Only `PATH` and the locale were carried over,
  so a `JAVA_HOME`, `MAVEN_OPTS`, `GOPATH` or version-manager variable exported in `~/.bash_profile` (or
  `~/.zprofile`, `~/.profile`) was missing from builds, runs, Git and language servers on the host. Every
  variable the profile adds is now passed on, except the session's own (prompt, history, `SSH_*`, display).
- **Each project window acts on its own project.** Back in a project's window after opening another project, several
  things used the other one: a Typst file's `#import` root, where the Markdown lint configuration and
  `http-client.env.json` are looked up, **Project: Edit Settings**, the Project tree put back after **Remote:
  Disconnect**, exporting or importing run configurations, a template's `${projectName}`, the folder a new file or a
  new project is offered, the file finder's starting folder, and where a stack trace's or a CI log's files are
  found. A recent file of another project opened in this window after focusing that project's; it now opens in that
  project's window, where it was last left.
- **Snippets: `$WORKSPACE_FOLDER` and `$WORKSPACE_NAME`** named the project of the window opened last, not the one the
  snippet was typed in: back in a project's window after opening another project, they expanded to the other one.
- **The AI agent works in its own window's project.** Started in a project's window after another project had been
  opened, it worked in the other project: that was its working folder and the boundary of the files it could read
  and write.
- **ed25519 keys work for remote folders.** A login whose only key is ed25519 — what `ssh-keygen` makes by
  default — failed with "No more authentication methods available", and a server offering only an ed25519
  host key could not be reached at all. Editora now ships Bouncy Castle, which the SSH library needs for them.
- **A remote connection that goes silent is noticed.** Editora asks the server "are you there?" every 30 s
  and now gives up after three unanswered asks (about a minute and a half), so a network that drops packets
  instead of refusing them no longer leaves a window holding a dead folder until TCP times out.
- **Starting a program on a host right after stopping another is no longer refused.** The place the stopped
  one held is freed a moment after the stop; a start waits up to 5 s for it instead of reporting that too
  many programs are running.
- **Git in a project window with no file open** followed the project of the last window focused, not its own: once
  another project's window had been used, closing this window's last tab made it say "Not a Git repository" and
  refuse every Git command.
- **Remote:** trusting a folder on a server no longer also trusts the local folder with the same path (and the
  other way round). `Remote: Disconnect` now closes the SSH connection, not only its file channel.
- **Previews:** the floating Editor / Split / Preview toggle covered the right end of the HTTP response panel's
  toolbar (hiding Clear and Save response), the CSV grid's toolbar and the first row of the JSON / YAML / XML tree.
  Those previews now start below the toggle, as the Markdown preview already did.
- **Settings ▸ Sync:** the reason Connect was refused (no repository or branch, an unreachable repository, a
  GitHub error) could be replaced by "Not connected." a moment later, when the GitHub sign-in check finished. It now
  stays until the repository is edited, Connect is tried again, or sync is disconnected.
- **Markdown Lint: Lint Project** showed no results when the Lint tool window was closed: opening the window
  cancelled the scan it was opened for. A `.markdownlint` file saved twice in quick succession could be read from a
  stale cache. A lint squiggle could be left where the text used to start when the gutter was sized after the
  first paint.
- **Word and OpenDocument and PDF exports** dropped the text of a wiki link; it is now written as a link.
- **Markdown Lint: Fix Issues no longer rewrites code.** Indented code blocks, fences nested in lists and block
  quotes, HTML blocks and comments, and YAML or TOML front matter are left exactly as written, by lint and by Fix.
  A closing fence with an info string no longer flips code and prose for the rest of the file. MD026 no longer cuts
  an HTML entity; a directive that names a rule by its alias no longer disables every rule; a config file with a
  comment is no longer ignored. Fix keeps the caret and scroll position. The Lint tool window follows the active
  tab. Squiggles are drawn on empty lines and on each row of a wrapped line. Lint messages are translated.
- **Math is recognised when the document is parsed**, in the preview and in the HTML, clipboard, Word,
  OpenDocument and PDF outputs alike: `\,`, `\\`, `\{` and `*` inside a formula survive, multi-line `$$` blocks
  render everywhere, shell variables in prose (`$HOME/bin:$PATH`) and `$…$` inside code are no longer taken for
  formulas. Math and Mermaid diagrams are drawn for the preview's own theme.
- **The Markdown preview no longer rebuilds the whole document on every edit.** An edit rebuilds the block it
  touches; a long document is built a slice at a time. Long inline code wraps instead of being clipped; a missing
  image shows its alt text; a changed local image is reloaded; image paths with `%20`, `?raw=true` or a leading
  `/` resolve; a document with one very long line keeps its live preview. Right-clicking a link no longer opens it.
  Remote images are fetched from the address that was checked.
- **Word and OpenDocument exports** write a soft line break as a space, so paragraphs reflow. File: Open Last
  Exported File opens office and HTML exports. Exported HTML forbids scripts.
- **Markdown source:** front matter and inline HTML are highlighted; strikethrough, quotes, list markers and table
  pipes are styled; Kotlin, TOML and Mermaid fences are highlighted. Folding, the outline, spell check and list and
  table editing share one reading of code fences, front matter and HTML blocks, so `~~~` fences, nested fences and
  commented-out headings are handled the same everywhere. The outline and table of contents show a heading's text
  without its markup, and their anchors match the exports. Spell check covers link text and image alt text and
  skips front matter.
- **Markdown editing:** line-wise commands stop at the selection's last line and skip blank lines; inline toggles
  no longer produce markup that does not render; Enter in the middle of a table no longer splits the row; table
  keys leave code blocks alone and work in block-quoted tables; columns align for CJK text; dragging a web link
  onto a document inserts a link instead of saving the page as an image; block snippets (`note`, `tip`, …) expand
  only at the start of a line; table commands say why they cannot apply.
